newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: MANILA BOURSE SETS PENALTIES ON OWNERSHIP RULES.
newsitem.headline: MANILA BOURSE SETS PENALTIES ON OWNERSHIP RULES.

text.p: The Philippine Stock Exchange (PSE) said on Tuesday it had set penalties on members who do not comply with the minimum shareholders requirement and the foreign ownership rule report.

PSE president Jose Luis Yulo said in a circular that the stock exchange will suspend the trading of shares of a company that do not comply with the minimum 500 stockholders rule within 30 days after the bourse has notified it to do so.
The minimum shareholders rule ensures that the companies remain public.

Yulo said the bourse will impose a penalty of 10,000 pesos for every week that a listed firm fails to submit a report on the foreign ownership level which is usually limited up to 40 percent of a company.
The PSE also came up with new rules on the declassification of shares.
Firms which have declassified shares or have been listed with one class of shares, will not be allowed to reclassify shares, the PSE said.

The PSE had been encouraging firms to have only one class of shares to prevent price arbitrage. Most firms list A and B shares. Foreigners can only buy the B shares, resulting in a more expensive price than the A share.
Moreover, a company with a par value of one peso per share will also not be allowed to reduce it, the PSE said.
